summary: A biased-erasure qubit is demonstrated in a single 3D superconducting cavity using the vacuum and two-photon Fock states ($|0_L\rangle = |0\rangle$, $|1_L\rangle = |2\rangle$), achieving an erasure bias ratio exceeding 265 and converting over 99.3% of leakage errors into detected erasures with a transmon ancilla. After postselection against erasures, the qubit exhibits a strong error hierarchy with logical relaxation and dephasing rates of $(6.2~\mathrm{ms})^{-1}$ and $(3.1~\mathrm{ms})^{-1}$ exceeding the erasure rate by factors of 31 and 15, yielding a coherence gain of 6.0 beyond the break-even point and a residual single-qubit gate error of $2.9 \times 10^{-3}$.
motivation: Biased-erasure qubits promise lower thresholds and reduced overhead when concatenated into stabilizer codes exploiting their structured noise, yet prior experimental demonstrations in cavity QED platforms remained elusive.
method: A hardware-efficient $0N$ erasure qubit is encoded in two Fock states of a single coaxial stub cavity ($T_{1,c} = 0.47$ ms) coupled to a transmon ancilla with $\chi_{qc}/2\pi = 1.69$ MHz for mid-circuit erasure detection via photon-number parity measurement and logical gates via quantum optimal control pulses.
result: Logical state assignment error below 1%, false-positive and false-negative erasure detection rates of $(0.22 \pm 0.02)\%$ and $(0.69 \pm 0.03)\%$ respectively; postselected effective logical errors of $(6.2~\mathrm{ms})^{-1}$ (relaxation) and $(3.1~\mathrm{ms})^{-1}$ (dephasing) demonstrate a strong error hierarchy enabling fault-tolerant quantum computation via code concatenation.
